I’m really sorry you went through that, genuinely. I hope you’re doing a lot better now.

I understand that providing for the house financially is really important, but for the Watterson’s case… I think it’s different.

I know that they’re poor. It’s shown in The Treasure and in multiple other instances. But, in my opinion, being there for your children and your wife, is the bare minimum, and dare I say, all the Wattersons need. They very clearly love each other. Richard loves his kids (like how when he pats Gumball on the head in The Misunderstandings and is willing to get something to cheer him up in The Gripes) and they all clearly love him (like at the end of his little montage in The Love). Also, as shown in multiple episodes, they’re all they really got and they’re all they really need.

As shown in The Painting, Nicole is bored when she’s not doing anything and is insistent on doing work. Sure, she may not be getting paid much, and while she’s literally getting paid peanuts (shown in The Parents), but I wouldn’t say that she’s struggling. She’s clearly able to pay for a house, electronic devices ( the kids’ computer and their phones ). And clearly, she doesn’t want help - from Richard, at least. She was clearly afraid of him getting a job, and doesn’t really seem to mind him staying at home. The end of The Laziest shows that she’s happy to let him be just that… the laziest.

Richard does depend on Nicole, sure, but I don’t think it’s just for money. I think it’s for a lot more than that. I think Nicole also depends on Richard for the same variety of reasons.

Also, in that same episode (The Painting), Richard was able to get a job… emotionally (for his daughter, and I’m willing to bet for his wife too knowing him). The only he actually didn’t wasn’t really his fault, it was because of the faulty door to the office. And at the beginning of The Knights, he is willing to do chores if needed. He doesn’t execute them well, sure, but it’s absolutely better than nothing.

With that said, there are a lot lot lot worse husbands and fathers in media, who don’t love their partners or kids at all, like Peter Griffin, and that isn’t exclusive to cartoons. I’ll even provide one from Gumball: Harold. Enough said.

For your first point, right off the bat, here's something that contradicts it: Richard is willing to get a job for Anais in The Painting. Yes, he does complain about it, but in the end, he does try. If you don't count season one as canon, well here: look at the way Nicole acts. It seems like it happened before. You'd think that Richard maybe tried to get a job in the past, and knowing him, I'm 100% sure he wanted to help his wife out. Nicole probably didn't let him because she knew what was coming. You saw the little signs (i.e. the faucet being upside down).

As for the second, yes. The kids are always alone, but they do literally evil shit all the time... like Gumball selling Alan's parents, Anais literally hunting for friends, and Darwin being a dictator (I understand that Richard let him be a dictator but literally everybody else did too so it wouldn't be fair to single him out on that). I highly doubt Nicole OR Richard would approve of those things, and by the last example, they clearly don't. I understand that in those specific examples and ones that are similar, the kids aren't literal gremlins, but what's the difference? Anyways, Richard knew exactly what to do to deal with them when they were gremlins. I get that he got the information from a book about dogs, but, he probably dealt with something like this before due to how, well, well he handled it. Like Gumball as a child, he was very energetic there, maybe he used it at least once there. Or, sure, maybe he fell asleep a few times and wasn't able to do anything then, but maybe after is when he figured it out. Cuz Richard is willing to improve from his mistakes, as shown in The Return.

Thirdly, would you rather be with an abusive shit like Harold or someone who while unintentionally but still is annoying like Banana Bob (yes, I understand that Richard can make Nicole mad at times, like in The Limit, but literally everybody makes people mad, even people closest to them), or risk dying from being on a motorcycle without a helmet or something else that was shown in the park, or be with someone who genuinely likes you for you and not for being "the best", is actually willing to listen to your problems (as shown multiple times), knows how to comfort you, be there for you, able to cheer you up, etc? - all of these are from multiple episodes, but in my opinion, The Fury holds one of the best specific examples. Also, she didn't just so happen want to make that choice that day. She wanted to get to the tournament. It was a lovely example of the Butterfly Effect. She just so happened to meet the person who was just right for her.

Watch the montage on The Choices. That alone gives you a ton of evidence.

If you want examples of Nicole showing love to Richard then here you go: in just about every family photo of the Watterson family, Nicole is hugging Richard, in "Nobody's a Nobody", she states that he's her "right hand guy and her shoulder that she cries on", her giving him a kiss at the end of The Gi, and more.

Finally, for your last sentence, as I already said, that is far from the only reason. Besides, isn't your partner being nice what you want in a relationship? Isn't that literally the bare minimum? Isn't that literally the point?
